main:
Why Do Dogs Kick After Pooping? Should You Stop It?

When a dog kicks the ground with their back legs after pooping, they aren't trying to cover it. It's known as a marking behavior that leaves an "I was here" message through paw scent and scratch marks. It's completely natural, so in most cases there's no need to stop it.

3 reasons dogs kick after pooping

ReasonExplanation
Paw scent markingDogs have sweat glands in their paw pads. Kicking the ground is thought to rub that paw scent in and leave it alongside the smell of the poop.
A visible markThe scratch marks and scattered dirt and grass are said to act as a sign that "someone was here." It's a signal to other dogs that come by to sniff.
Relief and good feelingsSome dogs kick out of sheer excitement after a good poop, the way they shake themselves off.

Wild canids like wolves are also known to scratch the ground in a similar way. That's why many see it as an instinct passed down over a very long time. Some dogs scratch the air or the floor after going on a pad at home. It's the same behavior, so there's nothing to worry about.

People often think dogs do this "to cover their poop," but actually covering it is rare. Unlike cats, many dogs kick at a spot a little away from the poop.

Which dogs kick more often?

  • It's often said to be more common in unneutered males, but females and neutered dogs do it too.
  • Outdoor-only dogs do it more often on walks, where there's lots of scent information. Why dogs go only outside is covered in why do dogs only potty outside?.
  • Some dogs kick after peeing too. It's the same marking behavior.
  • Plenty of dogs never kick at all. That's not strange either.

Should you stop it?

In most cases, no. For dogs it's a natural way of expressing themselves. But in these situations, gently redirect them.

  • When they're tearing up someone else's flower bed or lawn: as soon as they finish, shorten the leash and move a few steps away.
  • When dirt or sand is flying at people: pick a potty spot away from the path.
  • On glass, thorns or hot ground: they can hurt their paw pads. On summer afternoons, check the asphalt ahead of time with the dog walk safety index.

When to talk to a vet

  • They limp or keep licking their paw pads after kicking
  • They drag their bottom on the floor (scooting) or keep licking their rear (it could be an anal gland problem)
  • Their poop looks different from usual. Check it with the dog poop color and firmness chart.
This article is general reference information, not a diagnosis. If your dog seems low on energy or has symptoms that worry you, talk to your vet.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do dogs kick the ground with their back legs after pooping?

It's known as a marking behavior that leaves their trace through paw sweat-gland scent and scratch marks. Some dogs also kick because they feel good after a good poop.

Are they kicking to cover their poop?

Mostly not. Covering the poop is rare; it's closer to a marking behavior that leaves scent and scratch marks.

Should I stop my dog from kicking after pooping?

It's natural behavior, so in most cases you don't need to stop it. Only gently redirect them with the leash when they're tearing up someone's flower bed or the ground is unsafe.

My dog never kicks. Is that okay?

Yes. Lots of dogs don't kick. It depends on personality and habit.
